The modulus of a complex number is the distance of the complex number from the origin in the complex plane. For a complex number $z = a + bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers, its modulus $|z|$ is given by $|z| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.

The conjugate of a complex number $z = a + bi$ is $\overline{z} = a - bi$. Recall the property that the modulus of the conjugate of a complex number is the same as the modulus of the original complex number, so $|\overline{z}| = |z|$.

The modulus of the product of two real numbers is the product of their moduli. In other words, if we have the product $xy$, where $x$ and $y$ are real numbers, then $|xy| = |x||y|$.

Given that $|\overline{z}| = |z| = 5$, then $|\overline{z}^2| = |\overline{z}|\cdot|\overline{z}| = 5\cdot5 = 25$.
